[00:00] Sofia (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we planned about 45 minutes, is that still good?
[00:04] Maya: Yes, perfect, we wanted to focus on cost per token and what levers we have to keep within our monthly budget.
[00:12] Sofia: Great. Marco from our infra team will cover batching and caching later — he'll get into throughput and latency tradeoffs.
[00:18] Marco (Redwood SE): Hey all, quick hi — and I'll try to keep the deep math to a minimum, but feel free to interrupt.
[00:24] Olivia (CTO): Quick context: we run inference for summarization and signals extraction, heavy long-context prompts, about 200M tokens/month today but could double. Budget target roughly $8k-12k/month for model inference.
[00:40] Ethan: Our important constraints are p95 latency < 300ms for short queries, and batch jobs can be higher but they need throughput. Also need VPC and KMS for customer data.
[00:51] Sofia: Understood. For hosted per-token pricing, our baseline for the model family you're evaluating (open 7B-style / rlhf-ish) is $0.0025 per 1k tokens for generation and $0.0005 per embedding, but I'll send exact tier sheets. That baseline is where customers start on Hosted.
[01:10] Maya: So that number doesn't change with batching? It seems high if we go to 200-400M tokens.
[01:16] Marco: Right — the per-token line on hosted invoice is the software-side unit, but you can reduce effective unit cost dramatically using batching and KV/prefix caching. Two levers: increase tokens per GPU-second (batching), and avoid re-computing common prefixes (KV cache).
[01:32] Ethan: Can you give a concrete example?
[01:35] Marco: Sure — imagine 1k short queries where each is 50 tokens. If you do them 1:1 you'll have many tiny requests with overhead. With continuous batching we can accumulate micro-batches for a few ms, pack X sequences into GPU batch and get 2-3x throughput improvement, so effective cost per token drops. For some enterprise customers we've seen 30-60% cost reductions.
[01:56] Maya: What's the latency hit? We're sensitive for the interactive ones.
[02:01] Marco: For interactive queries we keep batching windows very small — like 5-20ms — and p95 increase is usually modest, e.g., from 80ms to 110-140ms depending on model and length. If you need strict p95 < 300ms you're fine; p99 is where it grows.
[02:15] Olivia: And KV cache?
[02:17] Marco: KV cache stores recent prefixes per user or per route. If you have repeated context (like templates, legal preamble, or system messages), we avoid re-encoding it. That can cut token compute by, say, 20-50% depending on repetition. It's very workload-dependent.
[02:33] Maya: For our summarization pipelines we have 30% overlap across prompts because of standardized preamble and stock templates. Sounds promising.
[02:41] Sofia: On Dedicated — if you reserve capacity, pricing moves to a committed monthly fee with included token throughput. Dedicated is for predictable, high-volume workloads and gives you cost predictability plus data isolation. We can model a committed tier that hits your budget range — effectively lower per-token equivalent if you commit.
[02:58] Maya: Do you have example numbers?
[03:01] Sofia: Example: a small dedicated pool starts at $Xk/month including Y tokens equivalent; beyond that we price incremental token consumption at a lower rate, and you also get access to priority capacity and lower throttling. I'll include a worked example in the sheet.
[03:15] Ethan: If we go Dedicated, can we still use KV caching and batching optimizations?
[03:20] Marco: Absolutely — same runtime features apply. In Dedicated you also get more tuning control — longer batching windows, pinned GPUs for large batch throughput, and more control over autoscaling policies. That can further reduce effective per-token cost because you squeeze more tokens per GPU-second.
[03:36] Olivia: How does Private (VPC / on-prem) change pricing?
[03:39] Sofia: Private has a platform fee + deployment fees (either bring-your-own-hardware or managed VPC instances). The per-token economics depend on your infra — if you self-host on cheaper GPUs and tune quantization aggressively, you can get lower unit costs but you take on ops overhead. We can help with quantization recommendations and kernel choices.
[03:56] Maya: We're also concerned about security compliance — SOC2, audit logs, SSO.
[03:59] Sofia: We provide SOC2 artifacts, audit log support, SSO/SAML, RBAC, and integrations with KMS/HSM. For Private we can integrate your KMS and retain audit logs inside your environment. We'll share the security pack.
[04:11] Ethan: For the benchmark you mentioned — what do you need from us?
[04:14] Marco: Ideally a 1k sample of your real prompts with distribution of lengths, expected p95/p99 targets, and an example embedding and generation mix. We'll run on both Hosted and a Dedicated-like config to show effective per-token cost and latency.
[04:28] Maya: We can provide that by tomorrow. Our monthly budget is soft but target is $8k/month for inference for now. If you show 40-50% savings with Dedicated+batching we may consider a commit.
[04:40] Sofia: Great — one thing to call out: hosted is easiest to start; Dedicated gives you predictability and lower unit economics at scale; Private is for compliance and potential further cost optimization if you manage hardware. We'll model costs in the sheet so it's apples-to-apples.
[04:55] Olivia: Any typical gotchas? Hidden charges?
[04:58] Sofia: Not hidden, but things that surprise teams: network egress for embeddings at scale, long-context memory usage (KV store sizing), and burst capacity overages if you don't set autoscale caps. We'll be transparent and include those in the example invoice.
[05:12] Ethan: For embeddings-heavy workloads, do you recommend caching embedding vectors?
[05:16] Marco: Yes — caching vectors or using a vector DB reduces calls to model for repeated vectors. If you have a high reuse rate, embedding cost can drop significantly. Also batching embed requests gives GPU efficiency too.
[05:28] Maya: Let's talk success metrics: what would you measure in your benchmark?
[05:31] Marco: Tokens/sec, cost per 1M tokens (effective after batching/caching), p50/p95/p99 latency, GPU utilization, and KV cache hit rate. We'll provide a spreadsheet with scenarios: hosted baseline, hosted + caching/batching, dedicated small commit, private on 1-2 node config.
[05:50] Sofia: Next steps recap: we'll send pricing sheet, Marco will run the benchmark once you send the prompt sample and token distribution, and we'll set up an infra call for VPC/KMS.
[05:59] Maya: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[06:02] Olivia: Quick Q — if we want to start with hosted then move to Dedicated, how painful is migration?
[06:07] Marco: Low friction — same API and model variants. We support pinning model versions and automatic fallback to hosted if Dedicated capacity is saturated during migration.
[06:18] Sofia: I'll follow up with calendar invites and the pricing doc. Thanks all.
[06:21] End recording.
